newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian 1997 oil exploration seen climbing.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian 1997 oil exploration seen climbing.

text.p: Australian petroleum and development activity is forecast to increase significantly in 1997 from the year before, the Australian Petroleum Production and Exploration Association (APPEA) said on Friday.
Projected development expenditure suggested activity would return to levels of the early 1990s, APPEA said in its 1997 activity forecast.
The rise in projected exploration activity largely reflected increased activity offshore, it said.

APPEA survey data showed that companies expected to spend between A$759 million and A$1.04 billion on exploration activity in 1997, with development expenditure forecast at between A$1.6 billion and A$1.7 billion and total expenditure at up to A$2.7 billion.
Of the total, up to A$2.3 billion was to be spent offshore and A$449 million onshore, it said.
APPEA deputy director Peter Cochrane said competition for exploration and development dollars remained intense world-wide.
Increased optimism on prospectivity, particularly in offshore northwest Australia, together with more buoyant oil prices, were likely to underpin projected exploration expenditure, he said.
Growth in development spending could be atttributed to recent exploration successes and further work on existing oilfields.
Expected activity levels were encouraging, but governments should not be complacent given volatility in trend figures and worldwide competition for funds, he said.
The Carnarvon Basin in Western Australia remained the most active offshore area with up to 44 percent of offshore exploration expenditure and up to 68 percent of offshore development expenditure.

The strongest performing area for onshore exploration and development activity continued to be the Cooper/Eromanga Basins in Queensland and South Australia, with up to 64 percent of onshore exploration expenditure and up to 74 percent of onshore development expenditure.
Drilling activity was forecast to increase, particularly in the Carnarvon, Gippsland and Cooper/Eromanga basins, it said.
The high level of seismic activity recorded in 1996 is also predicted to continue with an increase both onshore and offshore.
The survey showed that 57-76 wildcat wells were expected to be drilled onshore, together with eight to 20 appraisal wells.
Between 77 and 92 wildcat wells were expected to be drilled offshore, together with 17 to 30 appraisal wells.
Offshore exploration expenditure in 1997 was expected to be between A$589 million and A$841 million, while onshore exploration expenditure was expected to be A$170 million to A$196 million.
In development activity, 86 to 91 wells were expected to be drilled offshore and 41 to 77 onshore in 1997.
Offshore development expenditure was expected to be between A$1.33 billion and A$1.42 billion, while onshore development expenditure was seen between A$237 million and A$253 million.
